messages:
morgan: Heads up — observed a 2.6x tail on small-frame RPCs during the noon spike. Quick flame attached from the short-run profiler.

alex: saw that too. looks like tokenization + proto unpack is dominating for ~<128 byte> requests. CPU is burning in host-proxy before anything reaches kernel selection.

Priya: curious if this is kv-cache churn or pure parse overhead? can you paste the top hotspots?

morgan: top hotspots: 
- host_proxy::parse_frame (45%)
- tokenizer::tokenize_utf8 (22%)
- grpc_writev_coalesce (10%)
- kvcache::lookup (8%)
- http2::hpack_decode (6%)

jamal: small frames trigger repeated kvcache misses because we don't prefix-collapse early — index keys end up slightly different due to metadata order. that plus allocate/copy in parse_frame explains the extra cycles.

alex: repro script: 
```
for i in {1..10000}; do 
  curl -H "Content-Type: application/grpc+proto" --data-binary @payload_small.bin http://proxy:8080/stream
done
```
repro is cheap. can reproduce on canary.

sam: profiler timeline shows many 1–2ms spikes on parse_frame with stack walking into std::string allocs. we are doing repeated small heap allocations per message.

Priya: two follow-ups: 1) see if zero-copy proto parsing helps (reuse buffer and avoid string copies). 2) check if batching heuristics can aggregate tiny concurrent requests into one parse path before kernel selection.

morgan: tried zero-copy proto patch locally — parse_frame CPU down ~35% on the microbench. but kvcache miss rate increased slightly because cached keys were derived from ephemeral string view slices.

jamal: that's expected. we need a canonical key emitter that normalizes metadata ordering before caching. cheap stable hash of header set should do it.

alex: also noticed grpc_writev_coalesce isn't firing for these quick bursts because the writev window is too tight (flush on end-of-frame). increasing coalesce delay to 500us reduced syscall rate by ~40% on bench and smoothed tail. downside is +0.3ms median.

sam: tradeoff is acceptable if 99.9 falls. what about HPACK decode cost? for tiny frames it's nontrivial.

Priya: can we cache decoded header maps keyed by the same canonical header-hash? that plus reuse of header objects could drop HPACK time. we already have kvcache — reuse might be straightforward.

morgan: implemented canonical-hash + header cache on the local branch. initial results: kvcache hits up from 72% -> 88%, parse_frame drops 48% overall, tail p99 drops from 23ms -> 8.5ms on the spike scenario.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: proxy/canary-2026-03-21-14:30 (morgan)

alex: also surfaced kernel selection weirdness: for very short sequences we were immediately selecting int8 quant path because it advertised slightly lower token-cost. but int8 path has larger setup penalty on host which kills short requests. need to add a setup cost amortization term to kernel selector.

Priya: good catch. kernel selector should consider expected token count or expected latency budget when choosing quantized variants. propose: score = latency_est + setup_penalty / max(1, expected_tokens).

jamal: and batching heuristics: for small requests arriving within 1ms window, prefer coalescing pre-tokenization to avoid duplicate tokenizer work. keep an upper bound so latencies don't explode.

morgan: canary metrics look promising so far: syscall rate down 38%, p50 +0.25ms, p99 -60%. rolling to 10% now.

sam: action items: 
- alex: add kernel-selector amortization (PR)
- jamal: canonical header hash + header cache (PR open)
- morgan: publish microbench and attach flame, update perf-runbook
- Priya: run full KV regression bench against Dedicated configs

Priya: timeline?

morgan: aiming PRs today, roll to 100% tomorrow if no surprises.

alex: noted — will include a unit test for setup_penalty math.

jamal: i'll add telemetry for canonical-hash collisions and cache evictions.

morgan: thanks y'all. nice win — main takeaway: host-side costs (tokenize/parse/headers) + naive kernel selection together were amplifying tail for small-frame workloads. fix is combination of parse zero-copy + header canonicalization + smarter kernel scoring + a tiny writev coalesce window.

sam: +1 — please paste PR links here when ready and tag eng-sre for a soak run.

morgan: will do. :thumbsup:
